label: aival2-n2
_why: THE DOUBLED ai_value LADDER, TWO FULL-CENTURY RUNS (user-ruled 2026-08-20: 'double the ladder', n=2). ai_value = 1000 x (era+1) on every tier: e0 1000 / e1 2000 / e2 3000 / e3 4000 / e4 5000 / e5 6000, against aival-n4's 500 x (era+1). ARM: {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.aival2.json} - a full modded build, no overlay, no control. SPAN 1836.1.1 -> 1936.1.1, n=2, metrics identical to aival-n4, canon-n7 and the pinned vanilla baseline.
_what_this_actually_tests: ⚠⚠ READ THIS BEFORE INTERPRETING THE RESULT. Doubling is NOT a steeper ladder. The rung-to-rung ratio is IDENTICAL to aival-n4's - both are 1:2:3:4:5:6 - so if the AI weighs our tiers against EACH OTHER, this changes nothing and should reproduce aival-n4's null. What it does change is the tiered sector against the UNTIERED one. Measured field: 75 vanilla buildings carry no ai_value at all and therefore sit at the engine default 1000 - every farm, plantation, ranch, logging camp, oil rig, fishery, and the base light/heavy industry buildings; the raw EXTRACTORS (coal, iron, lead, sulfur, cotton, dye, opium, tea) run conditional blocks; only monuments (10000), the skyscraper (50000) and canals (100000) sit high. So aival-n4 put e0 BELOW that field (500) and e5 at 3x it; this arm puts e0 LEVEL with it (1000) and e5 at 6x. TWO PREDICTIONS, REGISTERED BEFORE THE RUN: (1) the below-best build-choice share should move LITTLE, because the rung ratio is unchanged; (2) the RAW SECTOR SHARE SHOULD FALL, because the whole tiered sector doubled against it - and e0 becoming relatively MORE attractive than a wheat farm (500 -> 1000) is the one direction that works against the stated goal. If (2) does not happen either, ai_value is a weak lever on both axes and the next attempt should not be another ai_value arm. Alternatives offered and declined for this run: 500 x 2^era (rung ratio 1:32, e0 stays below the field) and 250 x 2^era (same steepness, e0/e1 actively penalised) - both remain available if this is null.
_arms: aival2 = {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.aival2.json}, PAIRED with config/tech_tree_options.aival2.json (landmine L20). THE ARM IS THE CANONICAL CONFIG PLUS ONE FIELD: derived from config/mod_config.json at git db94b81 with a clean tree (sha256 D9512C19AEB7AA0ACC1E67D830269BA60BA0910EB17DE6AAD66D4E96D82238EB, byte-identical to canon-n7's frozen copy). A structural diff against the canonical config reports 104 differences and ALL 104 are industries[].tiers[].ai_value - verified by an explicit path test, not by eye; 99 of them read as type changes because the canonical config leaves the field undefined on every tier except tooling's six. building_ai_value is untouched (trade_center 5000, the one pre-existing entry). aival2's own sha256 is 6203EAADF9FFE18F70DD766AF537D770C34014C18503A0E68DAEE8CC248E999A. THE FREEZE IS LANDMINE L10 - all runs' build_state.json must show that sha before anything is reported, and no build-path file (build.ps1, preflight.ps1, telemetry_lib.ps1, emit_techs.mjs, emit_research_events.mjs, convert_history.ps1, extract_start.ps1) may be touched for the duration. NO CONTROL ARM, by standing user ruling.
_the_seven_that_do_not_get_it: As in aival-n4: 98 of the 105 tiers emit the ladder. power (3 tiers) and railway (4) are clone_from_vanilla industries carrying complex conditional vanilla ai_value blocks, which New-ClonedBuilding refuses to override (user ruling 2026-08-19: leave them out). Their vanilla blocks are unchanged, so in THIS arm they fall even further behind the tiered field than in aival-n4 - power's base value is 1000 and railway's 2000 against a tiered sector now running 1000-6000. That is a real, intended consequence of the ruling and a thing to watch in the infrastructure share. ⚠ It also makes power/railway a USEFUL CONTROL: they are inside the tiered taxonomy but outside the treatment, so a move in them is noise or a knock-on, never the lever.
_comparison: PRIMARY: against aival-n4 (20260819_215528, n=4, same game 1.13.11, same day, same machine) - this is the FIRST clean same-patch A/B this project has had on the ai_value question, and the only difference between the two configs is the multiplier. SECONDARY: canon-n7 (20260818_221216, n=6, 1.13.10) as the no-ladder baseline, with the patch caveat. TERTIARY: the pinned vanilla baseline 20260813_083557:vanilla (n=4, 1.13.10) for the G5 panels. ⚠⚠ THE NOISE FLOOR IS NOW MEASURED AND IT GOVERNS EVERYTHING: the below-best share runs sd 3.17pp over canon-n7's six byte-identical runs and sd 0.81pp over aival-n4's four. AT n=2 THE STANDARD ERROR IS AT BEST ~0.6pp AND PLAUSIBLY ~2pp; a move under ~3pp is not separable. n=2 is a scouting run, not a verdict - if it moves nothing, that is informative only because the ALTERNATIVE ladders are the next step, not because the null is established.
_watch: (1) THE RAW SECTOR, which is prediction (2) and the real point of this arm: extraction and agriculture share of levels built, absolute AND normalized, via analyse_build_allocation.mjs --a 20260819_215528_aival-n4 --b <this>. aival-n4 read extraction 1.06x and agriculture 1.06x against canon-n7, i.e. no starvation at all; if doubling does not move that either, the lever is weak on both axes. (2) The below-best share and its per-run spread (analyse_ai_tier_choice.mjs), against aival-n4's 50.52% mean / 0.81pp sd. (3) The era mix of CONSTRUCTION: aival-n4 moved e0 -3.49pp but sent it to e2/e3 rather than e4/e5, with e5 at 0.68x - does doubling reach the top rungs or repeat the middle-loading? (4) THE TWO G5 PANELS, now standing per-batch items: advanced_panel.mjs (productive share and GDP per productive worker, pooled GBR/USA/FRA/NET/BEL/PRU/GER) and tiered_panel.mjs (the same two inside the tiered industries). aival-n4 read productivity 1.113x vanilla and tiered workforce share 1.012x vanilla. ⚠ tiered_panel's productivity has NO vanilla denominator until the 2026-08-22/23 v6 vanilla runs. (5) Research-event firings as distinct (stage, tech, country) triples (L23) - aival-n4 5,113 across 79 techs, canon-n7 5,411/76; the bars are fed by predecessor-tier EMPLOYMENT, so a ladder that finally does suppress e0 should show here first. (6) Negative value added per worker in power (-£15), shipyard (-£11) and shipyard_steam (-£25), found in both mod arms at 1935 - shipyards are by design, power is not.
_cost: 2 runs x 100 in-game years. aival-n4 measured 2.56 / 2.67 / 2.50 / 2.57 h per run on this machine and patch, so ~5h10 plus 2 builds of ~8s and the concurrent save harvest. Disk: ~0.35 GB of retained session expected.
